description: Open Charge Map (OCM) describes itself as the global public registry of electric vehicle charging locations. The project README read on 2026-09-26 says it was established in 2011 to crowdsource a well-maintained open data set, mixing manually entered locations with imported open data from government registries and charging networks with open licences, and that it serves drivers through hundreds of apps as well as researchers, analysts and policy makers. The home page invites operators and national registries to supply data, including OCPI feeds, and offers the data through an API and embeddable maps; edits and imports pass through approval queues. The backend (API, web site and import processing) is open source in C# on .NET with SQL Server and a MongoDB cache. The site's API documentation and terms pages redirected to a sign-in page from this session, so the data licence and API key rules were not read. Caveats: completeness depends on contributors and imports, and charger status is not live. Simulation uses are siting charging demand in distribution grid studies and agent-based EV travel and charging models. Related records: data-france-sdirve-ev-charging-master-plans covers French charging planning.
